gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker Prime 160W's laptop-plus-phone output fell to 150 W (100 W + 50 W) after just over 40 minutes in Holger Becker's smartzone.de test, which is 94% of its 160 W rating. So under a long two-device load the laptop gets the same 100 W that UGREEN quotes for the 5-port Nexode Pro with up to three devices, at $50 per Anker port against $18 per UGREEN port at list price.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides (cited), Notebookcheck's US launch news (cited), Notebookcheck's 5-port review, the Anker US product page (cited), service.anker.com (cited) and our own Dealectric page (cited). For the Anker, Anker's pages give only a '160W max' total for two or three ports, with no per-port split and no measured sustained output. itechguides covers the 4-port UGREEN and gives no Anker price. Notebookcheck's news piece already states the UGREEN split of 100 W with 2–3 devices and 65 W with 5, so that part is not new. None of these pages has a measured sustained split for the Anker, or a $ per port or W per lb figure for both chargers. ChatGPT itself said it 'wouldn't declare a winner without controlled comparative testing'.
decides: It backs the value pick. Under a long laptop-plus-phone load, Becker measured the Anker settling at 100 W + 50 W. That is the same 100 W laptop figure UGREEN quotes with up to three devices plugged in. The Anker's extra $60 pays for size and weight (330 W/lb vs 201 W/lb), not for more laptop watts. For travel the Anker still wins on weight. For a desk the UGREEN gives the same laptop power at $18 a port instead of $50.
